citations.description: Docstring explicitly says runner.py LOC ceiling is NOT asserted
Only agent_call.py floor is asserted; no runner.py ceiling test exists

findings.criterion: tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py asserts runner.py is under 700 LOC AND that agent_call.py clears the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor — verified by that test passing.
findings.detail: The seam test explicitly does NOT assert runner.py < 700. The test file's module docstring states 'Deliberately NOT asserted: any ceiling on runner.py's own line count' (line 10), and there is no test function asserting a runner.py LOC ceiling. The test only asserts agent_call.py >= 100 and < 500 (test_agent_call_clears_the_split_floor, line 199). The runner.py < 700 half of AC3 is absent from the test suite.

citations.description: Third ticket comment by RebarBotNava: 'runner.py 658 LOC (from 699); agent_call.py 152 LOC' — method body LOC not mentioned. Commit SHA 8aa86fe097 is present.

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] The before/after LOC for runner.py AND for the PydanticAIRunner.run() METHOD BODY are recorded in the commit message. Evidence recorded on the ticket: a comment quoting both figures and the commit SHA that carries them.
findings.detail: The third ticket comment (the completion attestation) records the commit SHA (8aa86fe097) and the runner.py file LOC (699→658), but does NOT record the PydanticAIRunner.run() method body LOC. The criterion explicitly requires BOTH the file-level LOC AND the method-body LOC, noting the method figure is tracked separately because it has been repeatedly under-projected. The attestation is incomplete: the method body figure is absent.
findings.remediation: Add a ticket comment that quotes the PydanticAIRunner.run() method body LOC before and after the change (e.g., 'run() method body: 342 lines → N lines') alongside the commit SHA 8aa86fe097. The file-level figure (699→658) is already recorded; only the method-body figure is missing.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
